A minor triad will have the root note, a flat third, and a fifth.

There are no sharps between B and C. There are no sharps between E and F - think of a piano layout.

A minor triad will go root, 3 half steps and 2 whole steps - which is four half steps, obviously.

C - Eb - G

C (three steps) would be C# D D# (aka Eb) Eb (up three steps) would be E (no sharp between E and F) F F# and G.

So, your Cmin triad is a C Eb G. You can repeat some of those tones. C Eb G C is still a technically a Cmin triad. It's the number of tones - three distinct tones - that make it a triad.
